Thanks Dylan. Technical/ops clarifications below (flagging items that should remain conditional/legal-reviewed):

- Detection vs confirmation: We differentiate "detection" (we observe anomalous behavior) from "confirmation" (investigation validates unauthorized access/exfiltration). We avoid committing to customer notice before confirmation. Common workflow: detect -> triage (0-8 hours) -> confirm/scope (up to 24-48 hours) -> containment/remediation -> customer notification. In most cases, notification may be sent within 72 hours of confirmation; complex incidents can extend that window.
- On-call contact: Security Ops maintains an on-call rotation; for procurement portals we typically provide a primary incident email (secops@redwood.ai) plus a phone escalation for enterprise accounts.
- Artifacts: the attached evidence matrix lists the control families (IR, BC, IA) and sample artifacts we can provide (runbook excerpt, timeline templates, audit logs, forensic report summaries). We can deliver PDFs of redacted forensic summaries where appropriate.

Note: For GDPR-regulated data, Redwood will prepare artifacts to enable the controller (customer) to comply with their 72-hour regulator notification obligations; Redwood does not unilaterally file to supervisory authorities for customer data without explicit instruction.

-Karthik
Security Engineering
